text.p: Centennial Technologies Inc has reached a tentative settlement over pending class action shareholder suits filed against the company.
Centennial and certain officers and directors would be released from any liability in the matter, the company said in a statement on Wednesday.

The class action plaintiffs will retain their claims for the company's overstatement of earnings against the company's former chief executive officer, Emanuel Pinez, and the company's former chief financial officer, James Murphy.

In February 1997, Centennial said it would restate financial results for fiscal years 1994-96 and the first two quarters of fiscal 1997. The company had fired Pinez earlier in the month for insider trading, which later led to his indictment for securities fraud in March.
Centennial will pay to the plaintiffs the proceeds of any recovery from the company's directors and officers liability insurance policies, and an additional $1.475 million in cash.
Plaintiffs will also also receive thirty-seven percent of the company's common stock, which was delisted from the New York Stock Exchange in February 1997.

Meanwhile, the Securities and Exchange Commission's civil action against Pinez, who was denied bail on Monday for a third time, continues, according to Linda Bridgman, head of litigation for the agency's Boston office.

"The SEC does not have any actions pending against Centennial," she said, "But we do have a civil action against Mr. Pinez." Bridgman added that the action, which is also in U.S. District Court in Boston has been stayed pending the resolution of Pinez criminal case.
Bridgman doubted that the settlement in class action lawsuit against the company would have any effect on the criminal case against Pinez.
A number of issues remain to be negotiated regarding the settlement, including a binding agreement, Centennial said.

Plaintiffs have not yet reached an agreement with the company's interim chief executive officer, Lawrence Ramaekers, regarding claims by purchasers of the Company's common stock on February 25, 1997, but talks are continuing.
